pages.title: Overview
pages.purpose: High-level introduction to the Create_TF_feature_betacode project: its purpose, the problem it solves, key components, and how the pages below fit together.

pages.title: Project Purpose and Background
pages.purpose: Explains the scholarly and technical motivation for the project: what Beta Code is, that it is needed to be added to the N1904-TF datase to allow interfacing with legacy morphological parsers like Morpheus which depends on betacode. The created Text-Fabric feature will be included in the N1904addons ecosystem where it is playing a major foundational role.

pages.title: Repository Structure and Key Files
pages.purpose: Describes every file and directory in the repository (notebook, tf/ output, images/, .gitignore, LICENSE.md, CITATION.cff) and explains the role each plays in the overall workflow.

pages.title: Data Pipeline Architecture
pages.purpose: Overview of the ETL (Extract-Transform-Load) pipeline that converts the N1904 Unicode Greek text (i.e. each individual word/token) into its corresponding betacode equivalent (stored in TF feature called 'betacode'), linking to child pages for each phase.

pages.title: Environment Setup and Data Loading
pages.purpose: Details how the Jupyter Notebook environment is configured, how the N1904 corpus is loaded via the Text-Fabric API (use(), Fabric()), version pinning to 1.0.0, and the autoreload magic that keeps TF scripts fresh.

pages.title: Unicode-to-Beta Code Transformation
pages.purpose: Deep dive into the core conversion loop: iterating over F.otype.s('word'), retrieving Unicode text via F.text.v(), calling beta_code.greek_to_beta_code(), building the betaCodeDictionary, and handling edge cases (empty nodes, diacritics, capitalization).

pages.title: Feature Serialization and Verification
pages.purpose: Explains how the betaCodeDictionary is serialized to betacode.tf using TF.save(), the metadata written into the file header (createMetadata helper, provenance, license, version), and the verification step that reloads the dataset via N1904_ADD and checks A.isLoaded('betacode').

pages.title: Output: The betacode.tf Feature File
pages.purpose: Overview of the generated artifact and its role in the N1904addons ecosystem (namely to allow translaing back and forth between betacode and unicode), linking to child pages for format details and integration.

pages.title: Text-Fabric Feature File Format
pages.purpose: Documents the structure of betacode.tf: the @ metadata header fields (node, valueType, writtenBy, dateWritten, version, license, provenance, etc.), the line-based node-to-value data section, and how the TF engine parses and indexes the file.

pages.title: Beta Code Encoding Conventions
pages.purpose: Reference guide to the TLG/Perseus Beta Code dialect used in the output: ASCII symbol mappings for Greek letters, capitalization (asterisk prefix), breathing marks (parentheses), accent marks (slash, backslash, equals), iota subscript, and punctuation tokenization as seen in the actual betacode.tf data.

pages.title: Integration with N1904addons
pages.purpose: Explains how the generated betacode.tf file is side-loaded into the N1904-TF environment without modifying the core CenterBLC/N1904 dataset (it just adds functionality), the addons architecture, and how downstream users can load the feature alongside core features like lemma, sp, and morph.

pages.title: Exploratory Notebook (Untitled.ipynb)
pages.purpose: Overview of the scratch/research notebook used during development, linking to child pages for its two main concerns: the extended N1904addons feature set and the syntax-view query interface.

pages.title: N1904addons Extended Feature Set
pages.purpose: Documents the additional linguistic features available via the N1904addons module loaded in the exploratory notebook: betacode, translit, gloss, Morpheus analytic blocks (ma_class, ma_entropy, mm_num_blocks, mm_num_lemmas, ms1_–ms8_ summary groups), and how they complement the core N1904 features.

pages.title: Text-Fabric Search and Syntax-View Queries
pages.purpose: Explains the TF search DSL used in the exploratory notebook: the indentation-based query template syntax, node-type hierarchy (book/chapter/verse/sentence/wg/clause/phrase/word), N1904_ADD.search() and N1904_ADD.show() interfaces, hiddenTypes filtering, and the CSS-based syntax-tree rendering.

pages.title: Licensing, Attribution, and Citation
pages.purpose: Overview of the legal and attribution framework for the project, linking to child pages for the license terms and citation guidance.

pages.title: CC BY 4.0 License Terms
pages.purpose: Summarizes the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International license under which the notebook and betacode.tf are released: permitted uses (download, process, modify, publish, build applications), the attribution requirement (link to tonyjurg/N1904addons), no-additional-restrictions clause, and the as-is warranty disclaimer. Also covers the MIT licenses of the upstream dependencies (beta-code-py, N1904-TF).

pages.title: Citation and Academic Attribution
pages.purpose: Explains how to cite the repository in academic work using the CITATION.cff file (CFF 1.2.0 format), lists the author (Tony Jurg, ORCID), current version (1.3, released 2025-05-26), and provides the formal references for the upstream N1904-TF dataset (Zenodo DOI) and the Nestle 1904 source text.

pages.title: Glossary
pages.purpose: Definitions of all codebase-specific terms, domain jargon, abbreviations, and framework concepts that an onboarding engineer or digital humanist would need to understand when working with this repository.
